name: ADXL375 high-g 3-axis accelerometer
description: Analog Devices 3-axis MEMS accelerometer with a fixed ±200 g range and 13-bit output (49 mg/LSB), for shock, impact and crash measurements; I2C/SPI interface, shock/activity detection on two interrupt pins. The chip runs on 2.0–3.6 V. Sold as: Adafruit ADXL375 High G Accelerometer (±200 g) with I2C and SPI, STEMMA QT (#5374; 6-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, INT plus 4-pin header GND, I2, SDO, CS; 3.3 V regulator, 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups with level shifting, 3.3–5 V), I2C address 0x53 (0x1D with SDO high).
eli5: Measures very hard bumps and crashes (up to 200 times the pull of gravity) along three directions (X, Y and Z).

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3.3–5 V into the onboard 3.3 V regulator; also sets the SDA/SCL logic level

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the onboard regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board, 3–5 V logic)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board, 3–5 V logic)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: INT1 interrupt output (3.3 V logic, not level shifted), not needed for basic use

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Ground (first pin of the second 4-pin header, printed GND)

pins.name: I2
pins.description: INT2 interrupt output (3.3 V logic, not level shifted), not needed for basic use

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: ALT ADDRESS / SPI MISO: low on the board = 0x53; tie to 3.3 V (3Vo) for 0x1D. 3.3 V logic only

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select: tied to 3 V on the board = I2C mode; pulling it low selects SPI. Leave unconnected for I2C

supplierQuery: Adafruit 5374 ADXL375 high G accelerometer STEMMA QT
buildNotes: The chip powers up in standby with all outputs reading 0: set the Measure bit (0x08) in POWER_CTL (0x2D) before reading.
Check DEVID (register 0x00) reads 0xE5 first; a different value means a wrong address or a loose wire. (The ADXL343/345 also read 0xE5, so DEVID cannot tell them apart.)
The range is fixed at ±200 g and 49 mg/LSB: write 0x0B to DATA_FORMAT (0x31), because bits D3, D1 and D0 must be 1 per the data sheet.
Read all six data bytes 0x32–0x37 in one burst so X, Y and Z come from the same sample; each axis is little-endian twos complement.

With 49 mg steps and up to ±6 g zero-g offset per axis, gravity (1 g) is only about 20 counts: this part is for shocks and impacts, not tilt. Calibrate offsets (OFSX/OFSY/OFSZ, 0.196 g/LSB) if you need them.
Default address 0x53 (SDO low on the board); tie SDO to 3Vo for 0x1D. Leave CS unconnected (tied high = I2C).
Only SDA/SCL are level shifted: INT, I2, SDO and CS are 3.3 V pins, never drive them from 5 V logic.

driver.code:
# MicroPython driver for the Analog Devices ADXL375 +/-200 g 3-axis accelerometer (I2C).
# Written from the ADXL375 data sheet, Rev. B:
#   register map table 15: DEVID 0x00 (0xE5), BW_RATE 0x2C, POWER_CTL 0x2D (Measure = bit 3),
#   DATA_FORMAT 0x31 (SELF_TEST 7, SPI 6, INT_INVERT 5, D4 = 0, D3 = 1, Justify 2, D1:D0 = 11),
#   DATAX0..DATAZ1 0x32-0x37 (twos complement, DATAx0 = least significant byte),
#   fixed 13-bit output, scale factor 49 mg/LSB (specifications table 1).
import time

REG_DEVID = 0x00        # reads 0xE5
REG_BW_RATE = 0x2C      # LOW_POWER bit 4, rate bits 3:0 (0x0A = 100 Hz, the reset value)
REG_POWER_CTL = 0x2D    # Link 5, AUTO_SLEEP 4, Measure 3, Sleep 2, Wakeup 1:0
REG_DATA_FORMAT = 0x31
REG_DATAX0 = 0x32       # 0x32..0x37: X0 X1 Y0 Y1 Z0 Z1

DEVID = 0xE5
MEASURE = 0x08
# DATA_FORMAT: bits D3, D1, D0 must be written as 1 and D4 as 0 (data sheet register 0x31);
# Justify = 0 (right justified with sign extension), INT_INVERT = 0, SPI = 0, SELF_TEST = 0.
DATA_FORMAT_VALUE = 0x0B
SCALE_G = 0.049         # g per LSB (49 mg/LSB, typ; 44-54 mg/LSB part to part)
STANDARD_GRAVITY = 9.80665


def _s16(lo, hi):
    v = lo | (hi << 8)
    return v - 65536 if v > 32767 else v


class ADXL375:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x53, rate=0x0A):
        """addr 0x53 with ALT ADDRESS (SDO) low (Adafruit board default), 0x1D with it high.
        rate: BW_RATE code (0x0A = 100 Hz). Max ODR is 800 Hz (0x0D) on 400 kHz I2C,
        200 Hz (0x0B) on 100 kHz. At 1600/3200 Hz the LSB of each word is always 0."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        dev = self._r(REG_DEVID, 1)[0]
        if dev != DEVID:
            raise OSError("ADXL375 not found at 0x%02X (DEVID 0x%02X, expected 0xE5)" % (addr, dev))
        self._w(REG_POWER_CTL, 0x00)  # standby while configuring (data sheet recommendation)
        self._w(REG_BW_RATE, rate & 0x0F)  # normal power (LOW_POWER = 0)
        self._w(REG_DATA_FORMAT, DATA_FORMAT_VALUE)
        self._w(REG_POWER_CTL, MEASURE)
        # Turn-on time is about 1.1 ms + 1/ODR (table 1 note 8): 11.1 ms at 100 Hz.
        time.sleep_ms(20)

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def raw(self):
        """(x, y, z) in LSB. One 6-byte burst read so the three axes come from the same sample."""
        d = self._r(REG_DATAX0, 6)
        return _s16(d[0], d[1]), _s16(d[2], d[3]), _s16(d[4], d[5])

    def read(self):
        """(x, y, z) acceleration in g."""
        x, y, z = self.raw()
        return x * SCALE_G, y * SCALE_G, z * SCALE_G

    def read_ms2(self):
        """(x, y, z) acceleration in m/s^2."""
        x, y, z = self.read()
        return x * STANDARD_GRAVITY, y * STANDARD_GRAVITY, z * STANDARD_GRAVITY

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from adxl375 import ADXL375

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
accel = ADXL375(i2c, addr=0x53)
while True:
    x, y, z = accel.read()
    print('X=%.2f Y=%.2f Z=%.2f g' % (x, y, z))
    time.sleep_ms(500)
